strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with intermediate bidiagonal coupling and uncoupling transformations between stages. Each stage does one all-reduce dispatch (8 total), with local element-wise operations for applying/undoing the coupling pattern. Represents the straightforward translation with maximum simplicity but no collective optimization.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather to potentially leverage better network topology utilization. Each of 8 stages dispatches 2 collectives (16 total). The bidiagonal coupling operations are applied on the scattered shards locally, trading more dispatches for potentially better bandwidth utilization on hierarchical interconnects.

strategies.name: Fused Bidiagonal Transform with Batched All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Stacks all 8 intermediate buffers into a single tensor and issues one batched all-reduce across all stages simultaneously, accepting the cost of materializing all intermediate states. This reduces to 1 dispatch but requires 8× memory and loses the dependency structure, so only viable if the bidiagonal dependencies can be rewritten as independent operations on extended state.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node structure by performing intra-node reductions (using shared memory or local all-reduce) followed by inter-node all-reduce for each stage. Each stage dispatches 2 collectives: intra-node + inter-node (16 total). Bidiagonal coupling computed after intra-node but before inter-node, reducing cross-node traffic by leveraging node-local bandwidth.

strategies.name: Pipeline with Overlapped Communication
strategies.desc:
Issues all-reduce for stage k+1 asynchronously while performing local bidiagonal coupling/uncoupling computation for stage k, using non-blocking collectives and explicit synchronization. Still 8 dispatches but overlaps computation with communication to hide latency. Requires careful buffer management to avoid race conditions between dependent stages.
